title: ‘It’s like the wild west’: how AI has rocked the literary world
summary: With authors losing lucrative deals and writers removed from prize shortlists, accusations of AI use are sending shock waves through the publishing industry. Is it too late to turn the tide on machine writing? T he romance novelist Coral Hart got her break writing books for Mills & Boon, the publisher of bodice-ripper paperbacks. In 2012, she decided to dip her toe in self-publishing. She felt drawn to dark romance, a subgenre featuring twisted, toxic love stories that was taking off online but that publishers didn’t want to touch. Three years later, things were going well enough that she decided to self-publish full-time. Kindle Unlimited, where Hart sells her books, rewards prolific writers: the algorithm favours those who can produce a new book at least once a month. Hart says she knows of authors who hire more than a dozen ghostwriters to keep pace. By herself, Hart can write 10,000 words a day, but AI could help her produce many more. Since 2025 she has written 370 novels under 21 pen names using AI, earning herself “high six figures”. Continue reading...
title_en: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
title_zh: “如同蛮荒西部”：AI如何撼动文学界
summary_en: AI use accusations are shaking publishing, with authors losing deals and writers dropped from prize shortlists. Novelist Coral Hart says she has written 370 AI-assisted novels under 21 pen names, earning high six figures.
summary_zh: AI使用指控震动出版业，作者失去合约、作家被移出奖项短名单。小说家科拉尔·哈特称已用AI以21个笔名写出370部小说，收入达六位数高位。

title: Art ‘must not be sacrificed on the altar of corporate profit’ Liberal senator says as AI policy debate rages

As Labor considers copyright changes in an AI policy suite including datacentres, online safety, energy resources and economic benefits, the South Australian backbencher added weight to mooted constitutional challenges as to whether watering down copyright law would be an illegal acquisition of property .
